title: Acyclicity of a sheaf with zero generic restriction
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $C$ be a curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves] (a separated scheme of finite type over $k$ of dimension at most one) which is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Then $C$ is irreducible [lem-pc-integral-scheme-irreducible]; let $\eta\in C$ be its unique generic point [def-sc-generic-point], [lem-sc-scheme-sober], and let $j_\eta:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)\to C$ be the canonical morphism ($\operatorname{Spec}$ of the residue map $\mathcal O_{C,\eta}\to\kappa(\eta)$ followed by the canonical $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{C,\eta}\to C$) [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $F\in\Ab(C_{\Et})$ be an abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] which is torsion [def-weil-pbc-torsion-etale-sheaf] and whose restriction to the generic point is zero: $j_\eta^{-1}F=0$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then $H^q(C_{\Et},F)=0$ for all $q>0$, in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text:
*Every point $x
eq\eta$ of $C$ is closed.* $C$ is irreducible [lem-pc-integral-scheme-irreducible], and every irreducible closed subset of $C$ has exactly one generic point [lem-sc-scheme-sober]; in particular $\overline{\{\eta\}}=C$. The space of $C$ is Kolmogorov: for $x
eq y$ the closures $\overline{\{x\}}$, $\overline{\{y\}}$ are irreducible closed subsets with generic points $x$ and $y$, so they differ by uniqueness of generic points; if, say, $y
otin\overline{\{x\}}$ (if $y\in\overline{\{x\}}$ and $x\in\overline{\{y\}}$ the closures would be equal), then $C\setminus\overline{\{x\}}$ is an open set containing $y$ and not $x$. The dimension in [def-sc-curves] is the Krull dimension of the underlying space [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] (the Lean class `IsCurve` states it as `topologicalKrullDim C ≤ 1`), so $\dim C\le1$. Let $x
eq\eta$. Then $\overline{\{x\}}
eq C$, for otherwise $x$ would be a generic point of $C$, hence $x=\eta$. So $U=C\setminus\overline{\{x\}}$ is a nonempty open subset with $x
otin U$, and [lem-sc-dim-one-point-outside-open-closed] shows that $\{x\}$ is closed.

source.place: ## Proof, first paragraph: 'the remaining points of its non-vanishing locus are closed points'; argument written by the agent

proof.text: *The support of $F$ consists of closed points.* Let $\bar\eta:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to C$ be any geometric point lying over $\eta$ [def-weil-geometric-point]. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field], $\bar\eta=j_\eta\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ for the field map $\varphi:\kappa(\eta)\to\Omega$ it induces, and $\bar\xi=\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$ is a geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] for $f=j_\eta$ and $\bar y=\bar\xi$ we get $F_{\bar\eta}\cong(j_\eta^{-1}F)_{\bar\xi}$, and the right side is $0$ because $j_\eta^{-1}F=0$ and a stalk is a colimit of groups of sections [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Hence $\eta$ is not in the support $\operatorname{supp}F$ of [def-kun-support] (which applies: $C$ is of finite type over $k$), and by Step 1 every point of $\operatorname{supp}F$ is a closed point of $C$.

source.place: Lemma 0F0M (lemma-zero-in-generic-point): the hypothesis is the vanishing of the stalk $\mathcal F_{\bar\eta}$; the passage from $j_\eta^{-1}F=0$ to it is written by the agent

proof.text: *Approximation by sheaves supported at finitely many closed points.* The field $k$ is separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed]: if $L/k$ is a finite separable extension and $a\in L$, the minimal polynomial of $a$ over $k$ is irreducible and has a root in $k$ because $k$ is algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure], so it has degree $1$ and $a\in k$; thus $L=k$. As $C$ is of finite type over $k$ and $\operatorname{supp}F$ is contained in the set of closed points (Step 2), [lem-kun-cp-approximation] (with $K=k$, $X=C$) writes $F=\varinjlim_{G\in I}G$ as the filtered colimit in $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ of the set $I$ of its finitely generated subsheaves, ordered by inclusion, with the inclusions as colimit maps; and the support of each $G\in I$ is a finite set $Z_G$ of closed points of $C$.

source.place: Lemma 0F1F (lemma-supported-in-closed-points), proof, first sentence: 'By Lemma 0F0N we can write F as a filtered colimit of constructible sheaves F_i ... whose supports Z_i are finite sets of closed points'

proof.text: *Each $G\in I$ is acyclic.* The finite set $Z=Z_G$ of closed points [def-weil-closed-points] is closed, so $U=C\setminus Z$ is an open subscheme with inclusion $j:U\to C$. For a geometric point $\bar u$ of $U$, [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-stalk-germ] gives $(j^{-1}G)_{\bar u}\cong G_{j\circ\bar u}$, and $j\circ\bar u$ lies over a point of $U$, which is not in $Z=\operatorname{supp}G$, so this stalk is $0$ [def-kun-support]. Hence the map $0\to j^{-1}G$ is an isomorphism on every geometric stalk, so it is an isomorphism [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative]: $j^{-1}G=0$. Every $z\in Z$ is a closed point of the finite type $k$-scheme $C$ with $k$ separably closed (Step 3), so its residue field $\kappa(z)$ is separably closed by [lem-kun-closed-point-field] (b). Thus $C\setminus U=Z$ is a finite set of closed points with separably closed residue fields and $j^{-1}G=0$, and [lem-sc-finite-support-acyclic] gives $H^q(C_{\Et},G)=0$ for all $q\ge1$.

source.place: Lemma 0F1F (lemma-supported-in-closed-points), proof: 'such a sheaf is of the form (Z_i -> X)_*G_i ... Z_i is a finite disjoint union of spectra of separably closed fields ... H^q(Z_i,G_i) is zero for q>0' (packaged in lem-sc-finite-support-acyclic, as in the Lean proof of IsCurve.subsingleton_H_of_genericVanishing, which applies Etale.subsingleton_H_of_isZero_upperStar)

proof.text: *Each $G\in I$ is torsion.* Since $F$ is torsion, every geometric stalk $F_{\bar x}$ is a torsion group, by [lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations] ((1) implies (3)). The inclusion $G\to F$ is a monomorphism and the stalk functor is exact [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact], so $G_{\bar x}\to F_{\bar x}$ is injective and $G_{\bar x}$ is torsion for every geometric point $\bar x$; by the same lemma ((3) implies (1)) $G$ is torsion. So $(C,G)$ for $G\in I$, and $(C,F)$, are curve coefficient pairs [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting].

source.place: ## Proof (the torsion hypothesis of the statement; needed only to apply the curve version of the colimit lemma); written by the agent

proof.text: *Passage to the colimit.* The poset $I$ (Step 3) is a filtered small category, $G\mapsto G$ with the inclusions is a diagram of torsion abelian sheaves (Step 5), and $(F,(G\hookrightarrow F)_{G\in I})$ is its colimit in $\Ab(C_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. By clause 1 of [lemma-weil-pbc-curve-filtered-cohomology] the canonical map $\varinjlim_{G\in I}H^q(C_{\Et},G)\to H^q(C_{\Et},F)$ is bijective for every $q\ge0$. For $q>0$ every term $H^q(C_{\Et},G)$ vanishes by Step 4, so the colimit is $0$ and $H^q(C_{\Et},F)=0$.

The proof now follows Stacks 0F1F: (1) every point other than eta is closed (new node lem-sc-dim-one-point-outside-open-closed, whose Lean IsOpen.isClosed_singleton_of_mem_compl is sorry-free); (2) F has zero stalk at every geometric point over eta, so supp F consists of closed points; (3) F is the filtered colimit of its finitely generated subsheaves, each supported on a finite set of closed points (lem-kun-cp-approximation); (4) each such subsheaf vanishes on the open complement and is acyclic by lem-sc-finite-support-acyclic (Lean closed: Etale.subsingleton_H_of_isZero_upperStar), which replaces the blueprint's finite-direct-image + zero-dimensional-cohomology argument by the unit's own node that packages it, exactly as the Lean proof does; (5) the subsheaves are torsion; (6) the curve colimit lemma lemma-weil-pbc-curve-filtered-cohomology (the node of the Lean open entry) concludes. The blueprint's first paragraph (sections vanish off finitely many closed points; 'F_eta tensor_A L' is not meaningful as written) is replaced by the general approximation lemma; the blueprint's citations lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-cohomology, lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact, lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit are no longer used directly. The torsion hypothesis is not needed mathematically (Stacks 0F1F and the Lean have none); it is kept since it is in the statement and makes the curve colimit lemma applicable.

tool_uses.why: Step 3: a sheaf supported on closed points of a finite type scheme over a separably closed field is the filtered colimit of finitely generated subsheaves with finite support (Stacks 0F0N); the blueprint's first paragraph argues this ad hoc, and no node of sk-prop-cd states it
Step 4: residue fields of closed points of a finite type scheme over a separably closed field are separably closed (hypothesis of lem-sc-finite-support-acyclic); no node of sk-prop-cd states it
Steps 2 and 4: (f^{-1}G)_{y} = G_{f(y)} at geometric points (Stacks 03Q1 (3)); generic sheaf fact, no node of sk-prop-cd states it

Step 6: cohomology of a curve commutes with filtered colimits; it is the node of the Lean open entry Scheme.H_map_isColimit_of_isFiltered on which the item's Lean rests, and the blueprint's lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-filtered-colimit (sk-prop-h2) is equally off-unit
